title: Can You Solve This Pencil Mystery?

creative.hook: Two clues about a four-hundred-year-old case of mistaken identity hiding inside every pencil.
creative.learningGoal: Know that pencil lead is graphite, a soft form of carbon, and never was lead.
creative.signatureMoment: The wooden barrel turns see-through so the hidden core can be seen running the whole length of the pencil.

researchSources.title: Pencils never contained lead — McGill University Office for Science and Society
How long a line can a pencil draw? — Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge

script.fact: Here you go. A single pencil can write forty-five thousand words!
script.intro: Hello, superstar. Can you solve this pencil mystery?
script.answer: The answer is graphite, and that was great thinking.

clues: People have called me lead for four hundred years.
I am carbon, and I hide inside your pencil.
funFact: One pencil can write about 45,000 words.

visual.alt: A whole pencil with the wood turned see-through, showing the graphite core running its full length
